title: Space Tech Briefing — September 14, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts and future explorers! This is your daily dose of cosmic wonder, live on September 14, 2026. Get ready to launch into the latest and greatest from the final frontier!

Before we look ahead, let's recap some truly stellar developments from earlier this week. First up, an exciting call to action from France's space agency, CNES! They've just announced a fantastic opportunity for all of us to get involved in the future of human spaceflight. French astronauts Thomas Pesquet and Arnaud Prost are both set to embark on distinct missions to space in 2027. And here's the cool part: CNES is inviting *you* to help name their upcoming missions! Imagine having a hand in history, giving a moniker to the next chapter of French human space exploration. Keep an eye on the CNES channels for how to submit your brilliant ideas!

And speaking of incredible views, our second highlight takes us deep into the cosmos, courtesy of NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, or TESS. This dedicated exoplanet hunter, launched back in 2018, has been diligently scanning the skies for worlds beyond our solar system. Just a few days ago, NASA unveiled TESS's most comprehensive and breathtaking view of the starry sky to date! This isn't just a snapshot; it's a vast mosaic, meticulously constructed from observations taken between April 2018 and September 2025. This incredible map stitches together 96 sectors of the sky, revealing nearly 6,000 colorful objects that represent confirmed or candidate exoplanets. It’s a stunning testament to TESS’s incredible work, mapping out our cosmic neighborhood one alien world at a time. What an absolutely dazzling achievement!

That's all for today's space briefing. Thank you for tuning in and staying connected to the ever-expanding universe of space technology. Have a stellar day, and keep looking up!
